title: The Burnt Ghost
premise: Tamsin Okonkwo, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies for refusing to falsify threat assessments, recognizes the interior of a listed safe house as one she helped design twelve years ago — and realizes someone is selling its secrets to a domestic terror cell planning an attack disguised as an industrial accident. As she investigates off-book, she discovers the leak is her former mentor and first love, Callum Reyes, who believes exposing the safe house network will force accountability for an operation that killed his brother. Tamsin must choose between loyalty to the man who taught her everything and the truth that stopping him means burying the same corruption forever. In the end, she thwarts the attack at a chemical depot outside Rotterdam, but lets Callum die believing she betrayed him, then hands her evidence not to any agency but to a journalist, finally paying the full price of survival: exile from the system she once served.
about_author: Emrys Nystrom is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade adjacent to security bureaucracies before walking away. They write thrillers about people trapped inside institutions, and live quietly somewhere with poor phone reception.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Tamsin Okonkwo, now scraping by as a risk consultant in London, scrolls property listings at 2 a.m. and freezes: photos of a Dutch safe house she designed in 2013, down to the panic room hinges. Her POV establishes exhaustion and hypervigilance. Emotional beat: dread masquerading as curiosity.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Tamsin's firings from three agencies, each for refusing to bend an assessment. Her POV shows how rule-following cost her everything. She reports the listing through official channels and is told to stand down within six hours. Emotional beat: the sick familiarity of being dismissed.

chapters.title: Stand Down
chapters.summary: Tamsin flies to Rotterdam anyway, using old contacts to reach the safe house before it's shown again. Third-person limited follows her breaking into her own design. She finds the panic room stripped and a fresh burn mark on the floor — someone rehearsed something here. Emotional beat: the past reaching out and grabbing her.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: Tamsin tracks the estate agent, a money launderer named Vos who sells more than houses. His POV briefly reveals he doesn't know his client's name, only a courier schedule. Tamsin lifts the schedule. Emotional beat: predatory competence returning like muscle memory.

chapters.title: Callum
chapters.summary: The courier route leads to a marina café where Tamsin comes face to face with Callum Reyes, her mentor and former lover, presumed dead since 2019. His POV shows genuine shock — and a decision to lie to her. He claims he's investigating the same leak. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground was never solid.

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Callum pool what they know: three safe houses sold, a pattern pointing to a target. Her POV wrestles with trusting him while cataloguing every inconsistency in his story. They recover a partial manifest referencing 'Haven-4' and a date eleven days out. Emotional beat: warmth laced with poison.

chapters.title: Haven-4
chapters.summary: Tamsin decodes Haven-4 as a decommissioned NATO fuel depot slated for demolition — perfect cover for an 'accident' with a casualty radius of two kilometers. Her POV delivers the analyst brilliance her agencies punished. But when she calls an old colleague, the tip vanishes into a black hole. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into isolation.

chapters.title: The Rewritten File
chapters.summary: Digging into the depot's safety records, Tamsin finds an assessment bearing her own name — altered, dated after her dismissal, authorizing the unsafe demolition. Someone has been wearing her career as a disguise. Her POV, cold fury. Emotional beat: they didn't just erase her; they weaponized her.

chapters.title: What Callum Knows
chapters.summary: Callum's POV finally opens fully: his brother died in a 2016 operation run out of the Haven network, ruled accidental, actually negligent. Selling the safe houses funds his exposure campaign — but the buyers are the terror cell, and he's lost control of the plan. Emotional beat: guilt calcifying into justification.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Tamsin tails Vos to a handoff and photographs the cell's operational lead, a woman called Mireille. Intercut with Callum destroying evidence of his own role. Tamsin's POV catches him burning papers and says nothing. Emotional beat: love as a liability she can't bring herself to cut.

chapters.title: Mireille
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Mireille alone, trading silence for details: the attack targets a summit delegation transiting near the depot, timed to look like a gas explosion. Mireille reveals she bought the intel from 'a ghost inside' — and describes Callum without naming him. Tamsin's POV shatters. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed by the enemy.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Dike
chapters.summary: Tamsin faces Callum on the sea dike. He admits everything except intent: he never meant for anyone to die, only to burn the network down. She begs him to help stop it; he refuses, insisting the attack will force the reckoning his brother never got. Her POV breaks and hardens. Emotional beat: grief choosing duty.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Alone, Tamsin reconstructs the operation from fragments: delivery route, timing, the ignition method hidden in demolition permits. She drafts a report — and realizes any agency she sends it to contains the leak that rewrote her file. Her POV plans around her own country. Emotional beat: the system cannot save her, so she won't ask it to.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Tamsin meets Dana Okafor, an investigative reporter who once quoted her anonymously. She gives Dana the corrupted-file evidence with instructions to publish only if she fails. First shared POV chapter, trust extended cautiously. Emotional beat: handing someone else your life insurance policy.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Surveillance montage: Tamsin shadows the depot, maps guard rotations, and discovers the cell has inside access via a demolition contractor. Callum reappears, warning her off — or protecting her? Ambiguous. Her POV wavers between hope and trap-detection. Emotional beat: paranoia wearing tenderness's face.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Mireille's people find Tamsin's hotel room turned over and a tracker in her coat lining — planted weeks ago, possibly by Callum. She escapes a snatch attempt in the train station, injured. Her POV, bleeding and clear-eyed. Emotional beat: survival costing exactly what it always costs.

chapters.title: The Last Safe House
chapters.summary: Tamsin hides in the original safe house from Chapter 1, using its remaining dead drops to intercept the cell's final logistics. She finds Callum waiting there — he chose the place because it's theirs. Final conversation before the endgame; he gives her the detonation trigger location and asks her to let it happen. Her POV: no. Emotional beat: farewell without forgiveness.

chapters.title: Four Hours
chapters.summary: Race chapter, tight third-person alternating Tamsin and Callum as the convoy approaches. Tamsin disables the ignition charge at the depot's pump manifold while Callum, torn, blocks Mireille's backup team — choosing her side at last, too late to matter cleanly. Emotional beat: two people doing the right thing in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Burnt Ghost
chapters.summary: Climax: Mireille triggers a secondary device; the depot ignites partially. Tamsin drags the wounded Callum clear, but he's hit covering her retreat and dies in the firelight, telling her the archive proving his brother's murder is under the floor of the first safe house. Her POV holds the moment without flinching. Emotional beat: the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Tamsin recovers Callum's archive: proof of the 2016 operation's negligence and the rewritten assessments, including hers. She must decide: destroy it to protect his memory, or release it and let the truth indict them both. Her POV, quiet and deliberate. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth, resolved at last.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Tamsin gives Dana Okafor everything. The story breaks across Europe; inquiries open; names she once served are subpoenaed. No agency offers her redemption, and none is asked for. Her POV watches from a ferry terminal as the news cycles. Emotional beat: justice that costs the witness everything but the truth.

chapters.title: Exile, Chosen
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Tamsin, under a new name in a coastal town, receives a letter from Dana — the inquiry has reached the top. She walks the beach where the sea keeps rewriting the shore, at peace with being the burnt ghost who survived by telling the truth. Final beat: the price of survival was everything except herself.
